To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coordination to the S-site of Met occurs first, and then the coordination of the N-site of His follows.
the formation of His–Met–Pt chelate is energetically favorable and the rate-determining step is the replacement of water molecules by the sulfur and nitrogen atoms.
the chelate structure of cisplatin with histidine and methionine is formed by the stepwise replacement of aqua-ligands by sulfur and nitrogen sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of formation of chelate complex of cisplatin with His-Met peptide.
the formation of chelate between His-Met peptide and cisplatin, which can be used as the model of interaction of the drug with the tumor cells.
the mechanism of cisplatin activation by dipeptides and the role of histidine and methionine residues in this activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chelating ability of cisplatin is not very strong.
the formation of cisplatin chelates with dipeptide is a spontaneous process, which can be accelerated by several orders of magnitude by the presence of a second nucleophile.
the chelation of cisplatin with His-Met peptide is a thermodynamically and kinetically favorable process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cisplatin coordination to the dipeptide proceeds in the order: N(His)–S(Met), S(Met)–N(His) and S(Met) with the energy barriers for the first and second steps of 8 and 11 kcal mol-1, respectively.
